story.title: ICC Judges Determine Duterte Fit for Trial Amid Cognitive Concerns
story.summary: Judges at the International Criminal Court have ruled that former Philippine President Rodrigo Duterte is fit to stand trial, set to begin in November. This decision comes despite arguments from his legal team claiming he suffers from cognitive deficiencies.

event_overview.title: About ICC Proceedings
event_overview.subject: ICC Proceedings
event_overview.summary: These proceedings concern the ICC case against former Philippine president Rodrigo Roa Duterte, arising from the Court’s investigation into alleged crimes connected with killings in the Philippines’ so-called “war on drugs.” The ICC has confirmed charges of crimes against humanity against Duterte and committed the case to trial; confirmation of charges is not a finding of guilt, which remains for the Trial Chamber to determine.

facts.label: Court and legal framework
facts.value: The International Criminal Court is a permanent court governed by the Rome Statute, with its seat in The Hague, Netherlands; it tries individuals, where warranted, for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity and aggression.

facts.label: Case scope
facts.value: The case concerns alleged crimes against humanity in the Philippines between 1 November 2011 and 16 March 2019, including alleged murder and attempted murder in the context of the “war on drugs” campaign.

facts.label: Jurisdiction
facts.value: Although the Philippines’ withdrawal from the Rome Statute took effect on 17 March 2019, the ICC has held that it may exercise jurisdiction over alleged crimes committed while the country was a State Party, through 16 March 2019.

facts.label: Procedural history
facts.value: Duterte was surrendered to ICC custody on 12 March 2025. On 23 April 2026, Pre-Trial Chamber I confirmed all three counts of crimes against humanity brought by the Prosecutor and referred the case for trial.

facts.label: Trial posture as of 8 October 2026
facts.value: Trial Chamber III found Duterte fit to stand trial, with participation measures adopted, and the opening of trial was scheduled for 30 November 2026.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers specific 2026 court appearances and fitness-to-stand-trial developments in Duterte’s case, not the full ICC investigation into the Philippines, the broader drug-war context, or all filings and hearings.

related_stories.title: Commemoration of October 7 Attack Amid Ongoing Struggles in Gaza
related_stories.summary: On the third anniversary of the October 7 attack, Israelis are gathering to mourn the loss of 1,200 lives and the taking of 251 hostages. Meanwhile, Palestinians in Gaza continue to face devastation, with nearly two million residents living in ruins due to ongoing conflict and strikes. Global protests are also occurring in solidarity with Gaza as the situation remains dire.

related_stories.title: British Police Acknowledge Unlawful Search Warrants in Case Against Former Prince Andrew
related_stories.summary: British police have admitted that the search warrants issued to investigate properties linked to Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor were unlawful and must be quashed. A London judge confirmed this ruling, although the investigation into the younger brother of King Charles II remains ongoing. Andrew was arrested on February 19 on suspicion of misconduct in public office.

related_stories.title: South Korea Recalls Ambassador to Ukraine Amid POW Dispute
related_stories.summary: South Korea has announced the recall of its ambassador to Ukraine following a diplomatic dispute over the public disclosure of the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war. The South Korean government expressed concerns that this revelation could endanger the prisoners' families in North Korea and has demanded an apology from Ukraine, which has not been forthcoming. The situation escalated after South Korean President Lee Jae Myung threatened unspecified punitive measures if Ukraine does not respond.

related_stories.title: UK Consulate in East Jerusalem to Transition to 'UK Mission'
related_stories.summary: The UK consulate in East Jerusalem will cease operations and be rebranded as the 'UK Mission, Jerusalem,' according to British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband. This change is set to take effect on Thursday, but the consulate building will remain in place.
